info.title: origin API
info.description: The repositories an origin server hosts: their records, targets, landing queues and events.

get.summary: Returns the OpenAPI document of this API.
Lists the repositories on the server.

401.description: The token is invalid or expired

post.summary:
Lists what the repository holds of some changes: their revisions,
heads and statements, by id.

200.description: An inventory for each change, in the order asked: empty for a change the repository never heard of

get.summary: Lists the revisions of a change, and its heads.

200.description: The revisions, in the order the repository received them

404.description: The repository or the change does not exist

get.summary:
Reads the events after a cursor, waiting up to `wait` for some to arrive (a
long-poll). Pass the page's `next` as the next request's cursor. While too
many long-polls are waiting on the server, a request first waits for one of
them to end, and that time counts toward `wait`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
The cursor to read after: the `next` of the previous page. Defaults to
the end of the stream, so only new events are returned.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description:
The generation of the op log the cursor belongs to, as its page gave it.
A cursor from another generation, such as from before the repository was
restored, has expired.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
How long to wait for events, such as `30s`. Without it, the server
answers at once, possibly with no events.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Roughly how many events to return. All the events of one op log entry are
returned together, so a page can exceed it.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Only return events with these names or statement kinds, comma-separated,
such as `check.requested,ci.*`.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description:
Only return events whose subject starts with one of these,
comma-separated, such as a revision id prefix, `change:3fa2` or `main`.

200.description: The events, oldest first, and the next cursor: empty if none came in time

410.description: The server no longer keeps the events after the cursor

post.summary:
Submits a change, or a target's tip, to a target's landing queue, which this
server runs.

200.description: How each landing went: landed, unchanged, or waiting for evidence or a conflict's resolution

400.description: A target was proposed without a target to land on

404.description: The repository, the change or a target does not exist

409.description: The change diverged or was abandoned, or this server doesn't order the target

get.summary: Lists the landings waiting, and why.
Lists the acceptances of a target, oldest first.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The position of the first acceptance to return. Defaults to 0, the first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most acceptances to return. Defaults to all.

404.description: The repository or the target does not exist

put.summary:
Puts a batch of objects as a pack: snapshots, revisions and statements. Each
may only need objects that the batch or the repository has, of the right
kinds. With `expect`, puts them only if the changes it names still have the
heads it gives when the records are published.

parameters.name: expect
parameters.description:
The heads of the changes as the caller saw them, comma-separated. Each is
`<change>=<head>+<head>`, or `<change>=` for a change the repository
didn't have. The batch is refused if any change's heads differ now.

400.description: The pack is invalid, holds an acceptance, or needs objects the repository doesn't have, or has as another kind

409.description: A change of `expect` has other heads now

post.summary: Fetches records by id as a pack, each with the attachment it carries.

200.description: The records, in the order asked, each followed by its description or payload if the repository has it, as a pack: each object a 32-byte id, a little-endian u64 length and the object's encoding. At most 64 MiB, but for a record alone

origin-more.description: Present if the pack stopped short: ask again for the records after the last it holds

400.description: An object is a blob, a tree or an attachment, which only leave by walking a snapshot or with the record carrying them

404.description: The repository or a record does not exist

post.summary:
Fetches the objects of a snapshot that the caller lacks, as a pack. This is
the only way trees and blobs leave a repository.

200.description: The trees and blobs, parents before children, as a pack, of at most 64 MiB, but for an object alone

origin-more.description: Present if the pack stopped short: ask again, skipping the objects it holds

404.description: The repository or the snapshot does not exist

get.summary:
Lists the statements about a record, in the order the repository
received them.
Lists the targets, with their tips, authorities and requirements.

post.summary: Creates a target at the tip of another, with this server as its authority.

404.description: The repository or the target to start from does not exist

409.description: The name is taken, or this server wouldn't order the target

post.summary:
Issues a token that acts for the caller, with a scope narrowing their
rights. The server signs it, and verifies it later without storing it.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: The repository whose policy the scope is checked against

403.description: The caller isn't signed in, or the scope reaches beyond their rights

get.summary: Tells the caller who they are and what they may do in the repository.

401.description: The token is invalid or expired

Acceptance.description:
One landing on a target, signed by the target's authority.

Each acceptance names the one before it on the target, forming a hash
chain, and its sequence number is its position in the target's log.

In JSON, it is the body's fields plus the signature in hex.

evidence.description: The statements the policy relied on.

oneOf.description:
The acceptance of the `policy` target in force when this one landed.
Absent only for the first acceptance of `policy`, which nothing
precedes.
The acceptance before this one, absent only for the first.

seq.description: The position in the target's log, from 0.

state.description: The target's snapshot after this landing.

Annotation.description:
A statement, whether its issuer superseded it, and whether its claim
holds.

holds.description:
Whether the landing queue would count the claim as evidence. It must not
be superseded. A promotion must also be valid, its original must not be
superseded, and no result about the record may replace it.

oneOf.description: The first statement from the same issuer that supersedes it.

ApiError.description: The error a request failed with.

oneOf.description: The state of a target after one of its acceptances.

acceptance.description: The state of a target after one of its acceptances.

oneOf.description: Another revision, such as the one below in a stack.

revision.description: Another revision, such as the one below in a stack.

Base.description: What a revision was made on top of.

oneOf.description: The subject lacks these statements, which the target requires.

evidence.description: The subject lacks these statements, which the target requires.

oneOf.description:
Both sides changed these paths. The `core.conflict` statement lists
them too.

conflict.description:
Both sides changed these paths. The `core.conflict` statement lists
them too.

cursor.description:
The sequence number of the op log entry the event comes from. Reading
from this cursor delivers the events of later entries.

Event.description: An event, with its position in the op log.

oneOf.description: A statement was issued.
Its verdict.
A revision was created.
A target advanced.

seq.description: The new acceptance's position in the target's log.

oneOf.description: A waiting landing lacks a statement it requires.

subject.description: The record the required statement must be about.

EventKind.description:
What happened: the event without its cursor. Consumers deduplicate events
by it. In JSON, the `event` field holds its name, as [`EventKind::name`]
returns it.

FetchRecords.description:
A request for records by id: revisions, statements and acceptances. Each
record comes with its attachment, if the repository has it: a revision's
description or a statement's payload. Fetch snapshots with
[`FetchSnapshot`] instead.

ids.description:
The ids of the records, which are returned in this order, each followed
by its attachment. A response with the [`MORE`] header stops short. Ask
again for the records after the last one it holds.

FetchSnapshot.description:
A request for the trees and blobs of a snapshot that the caller lacks,
walked from its root. This is the only way blobs and trees leave a
repository, so the server can check what each caller may read by path.

have.description:
Snapshots the caller holds in full. Anything one of them holds at the
same path is skipped, so only what changed is sent. Snapshots the
repository doesn't have are ignored.

of.description:
The record whose snapshot to fetch: a revision or an acceptance. Only a
record's whole snapshot can be walked, not a tree inside it, because the
tree's paths would be checked as if they were other paths.

paths.description:
Limits the fetch to these files and directories, everything under them,
and the trees on the way to them. Defaults to everything.

skip.description:
How many objects to skip, because earlier parts brought them. A response
that stops short has the [`MORE`] header.

Head.description: The latest acceptance of a target.

seq.description: Its position in the log, from 0.

Inputs.description:
What a statement depended on.

The input digest of a snapshot hashes the ids it stores at `paths`, with
`definition` and `toolchain`. A statement that declares inputs and isn't
`external` is promoted to every revision with the same input digest.

external.description:
Whether the claim also depended on things outside the snapshot, such
as the network, which makes it never promotable.

paths.description: The files and directories read, each covering everything under it.

toolchain.description: The tools that ran it, such as the hash of `rustc -V`.

Inventory.description:
What a repository holds of a change: the ids of its records, to compare
with another node's.

heads.description: The revisions that no other revision of the change evolves from.

revisions.description:
The change's revisions, in the order the repository received them. Empty
if the repository has never seen the change.

statements.description:
The statements about the change's revisions, and about those statements,
in no particular order.

InventoryRequest.description: A request for what a repository holds of some changes.

expires.description: When it expires, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

token.description: The token, to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

LandRequest.description: A request for the queue to land something.

oneOf.description:
The target to land on. For a change, defaults to the target its stack is
on. Landing a target requires it.
It landed.

source.description: The revision or acceptance the acceptance names.

oneOf.description: The target already has it, so nothing landed.

unchanged.description: The target already has it, so nothing landed.

oneOf.description: It waits, and the queue keeps it.

pending.description: It waits, and the queue keeps it.

landings.description:
The outcome of each landing: one for each change of the stack that the
target didn't have, from the bottom, up to the first one that waits.

Level.description: What a caller may do with a path.

LogEntry.description: One acceptance in a target's log.

acceptance.description: The acceptance. Its `seq` is its position in the log.

NewTarget.description: A request to create a target.

from.description: The target whose tip the new target starts at.

Page.description: A batch of events, and the cursor to read the next batch from.

generation.description:
The generation of the op log the cursor belongs to. Pass it along with
the cursor: a cursor means nothing in another generation.

next.description: The cursor after the entries read. Pass it to the next read.

PathAccess.description:
What a caller may do with every path. A path gets the level of the most
specific listed path at or above it. The root is always listed.

Pending.description: A landing that waits, kept in the queue to be listed and retried.

subject.description:
What the evidence must be about: the revision that would land, or the
merged snapshot when landing a target. For a conflict, the revision or
acceptance that did not merge.

oneOf.description: A change, as of its head.

change.description: A change, as of its head.

oneOf.description: Another target, as of its tip.

target.description: Another target, as of its tip.

RepoName.description:
The name of a repository on a server: ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`
and `-`, not starting with `.`.

RepoSummary.description: A repository, as the server lists it.

Requirement.description:
A statement that landing needs: of `kind`, with `verdict`, from one of
`issuer`, about what lands.

Revision.description:
One immutable version of a change.

Editing, rebasing or handing a change to someone else creates a new
revision of the same change, whose predecessors are the revisions it
evolves from.

base.description: What the revision was made on top of.

change.description: The change this is a version of.

deps.description:
The exact revisions this one requires: the changes below it in a
stack.

description.description: The intent, written for humans and agents.

predecessors.description:
The revisions this one evolves from. Two make it a convergence of
divergent heads.

snapshot.description: The root tree of the files.

heads.description:
The revisions that no other revision of the change evolves from. More
than one means the change diverged.

revisions.description: Every revision, in the order the repository received them.

Rights.description:
What a caller may do, resolved from the policy in force and narrowed by
the scope of their token.

admin.description: Whether the caller may land on `policy`.

annotate.description: The kinds of statements the caller may issue.

groups.description: The policy's groups the caller is a member of.

land.description: The targets the caller may land on, not counting `policy`.

paths.description: What the caller may do with each path.

oneOf.description:
Who the caller is. `None` for an anonymous caller and for the node's own
user.

scope.description: The token's scope, if the caller used a scoped token.

oneOf.description: A revision of a change.
Another target, as of one of its acceptances.

target.description: Another target, as of one of its acceptances.

Statement.description:
An attributable claim about another record: a check result, a review, a
conflict, an abandonment.

Statements are permanent. An issuer revises one by issuing another that
supersedes it. A promoted statement carries another one over to a record
with the same input digest, pointing at it instead of copying its issuer.

oneOf.description:
What the claim depended on, which lets it be promoted to revisions
with the same inputs.

kind.description: What kind of claim it is.

oneOf.description: Free-form details, defined by whoever owns the kind.

The statement this one promotes: its kind, verdict, inputs and
payload hold here too, because the input digests are equal. The
issuer is whoever promoted it, the original's stays on the original.

subject.description: The record the claim is about.

oneOf.description: A statement from the same issuer that this one replaces.
The outcome, the only field core interprets.

Stored.description: The result of storing a batch of records.

new.description: How many of the objects were new to the repository.

TargetInfo.description:
A target, its location, and the node that orders it under the policy in
force.

oneOf.description: The node that orders the target, if the policy names one.

requirements.description: The statements that landing on the target requires.

TokenRequest.description: A request for a token with a narrower scope, for an agent or a CI runner.

scope.description: What the token may do: a subset of what the caller may do.

ttl.description: How long the token lasts, such as `1h`.
